beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Om Mali. This video is about measuring a local language model against the rule based matcher that already works, and reporting honestly when the model loses. Week five of the Private AI Valuation Agent. I gave an eight billion parameter model exactly the evidence the rules get. It lost. And measuring that properly is the whole week.

show.event: Cream Claude composer, empty. Serif greeting 'Hallo, HAI' + terracotta spark above it.
The ask types itself into the composer, character by character.
Send button arms terracotta; running indicator reads 'scoring 322 calls…'.
Three output lines land in sequence — the ask arrives ANSWERED (COLD OPEN LAW).

props.segment: Measuring a Local LLM Against the Matcher
props.command: Replace my deterministic matcher with a local 8B language model. Give it exactly what the rules get, score it against the same 322 labelled names, and tell me straight whether it earns the swap.
output: and it was fully confident on 12 of the 15 it got wrong

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole result before I show you any of it. The rules keep the job. A local model, given the same four fields and the same candidate list, was wrong in exactly one direction. It promoted holdings to companies they were not. Precision fell about five points. Recall did not move at all. I kept the rules, and this week is me showing you why.

shot.visual_intent: The BLUF: which system ships, by how much, and in which direction the model is wrong.

show.event: Headline sets in serif at display size, centred.
Two system cards land side by side; the incumbent takes the accent.
A delta bar drops between them, labelled −5.1 points.
A flat steady line lands beneath it, unchanged.
The verdict band stamps NOT ADOPTED across the foot.

props.headline: The rules keep the job.
props.directionNote: All 14 new errors ran one way: a holding promoted to a company it is not. Removals: 1.

beats.narration_text: Both systems see the same evidence. The name on the filing. The security title. The fund that filed it. And a list of eleven candidate companies, the seven in the universe plus four on the watchlist. Nothing else. No price, and no answer. Three hundred and twenty-two calls, on my own machine, about three seconds each. Zero failures.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w5-setup.png. The point is parity of evidence, so the four fields land first and the withheld pair is struck.

show.event: The four given fields land one at a time as labelled cards.
Two withheld chips — price, the answer — draw struck-through in ghost.
The run stats count up: 322 calls, 0 failures, 3.24s, 17 min.

props.sparkLine: Same evidence, or the comparison means nothing.
props.title: Exactly what the rules get
props.subtitle: one real golden-set row, as it reached the model

fields.label: security title
fields.value: HYPERSCALE DATA INC - SERIES F EXCH PREFERRED

props.withheldNote: Withheld from both systems. The model gets no evidence the rules do not.

beats.narration_text: The rules score ninety-nine point six percent precision. The model, ninety-four point five. Five points sounds survivable. Count it in records instead of cases, and it is not. One wrong record becomes a hundred and ninety-six. Same labels, same holdings, one system swapped out for another. That is the entire comparison.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w5-scoreboard.png. Precision first, then the same error re-counted in records — the unit switch IS the argument.

show.event: Two precision rows set at display size, the incumbent in terracotta.
The frame switches unit: the same two rows re-count as records, 1 and 196.
The 196 bar runs the full column width against the 1.
A steady line confirms recall unchanged at 1.0000.

props.title: Five points, in records
props.subtitle: same 322 labels, same 5,935 true holdings, one system swapped
props.multiplierNote: 14 wrong cases instead of 1, but a case is a name and a name can carry hundreds of holdings.
props.steady: Recall unchanged: 1.0000 → 1.0000. Nothing was lost. Things were added.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week5.json — scoreboard, macro and micro over the same golden set

beats.narration_text: It fails the same way every time. It promotes resemblances. It saw a company called Hyperscale Data and answered Scale A I. Its reason, in its own words: Hyperscale Data is the parent company of Scale A I. That is not true. There is no such relationship. The model did not misread the filing. It invented a corporate fact, and then reported it at ninety-five percent confidence.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w5-failures.png, first row. The model's own sentence is the evidence, so it is quoted and then struck.

show.event: The filed name sets at display size.
An arrow carries it to the model's answer; the true label lands beneath in ghost.
The model's reason types in verbatim as a quotation.
The parent-company clause is struck through and a rebuttal lands under it.
The confidence dial fills to 0.95 beside the struck reason.

props.title: It invented a corporate fact
props.reason: The issuer name is HYPERSCALE DATA INC, which is the parent company of Scale AI, Inc.
props.strikeFrom: which is the parent company of
props.rebuttal: No such relationship exists. Neither company is a parent of the other.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week5.json — failures[0], golden-set row g0191

beats.narration_text: Then a loan. Scaled Agile Incorporated, twenty twenty-one unitranche term loan. Also Scale A I, at full confidence, because the words look alike. That one is not a single record. Thirty-two holdings carry that name, and every one of them would have been priced as a company it has nothing to do with.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w5-failures.png, second row. The shared substring is lit in BOTH strings so the mechanism is visible, not asserted.

show.event: The filed string sets across the frame; the four shared characters light terracotta.
The answer lands beneath with the same characters lit — the overlap is the whole reason.
The confidence chip resolves to 1.000.
Thirty-two record marks fill a block and the running count steps 1 → 33.

props.sparkLine: The words look alike. That is the whole reason.
props.title: A resemblance, priced
props.filed: SCALED AGILE INC. 2021 UNITRANCHE TERM LOAN
props.reason: The issuer name and title match the name of Scale AI, Inc.
props.kicker: A term loan is not an equity stake in anything. The name is the only thing they share.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week5.json — failures[1], golden-set row g0254

beats.narration_text: And then this one. The filed name is X A I three, F T five O, dot A F. That is an internal Fidelity security code. It is not a ticker, and it is not a company name. The model answered X A I, at full confidence, on three matching characters. Eight holdings. There was never anything there to find, and it found something anyway.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w5-failures.png, third row. The script asks for this one ALONE on screen — nothing competes with it.

show.event: The code sits ALONE on the cream, character by character in a slot row.
Exactly three slots light terracotta; the rest stay ink.
The note lands beneath, small.
The answer, the reason and 1.000 land together at the foot.

props.sparkLine: There was nothing there to find.
props.codeNote: an internal Fidelity security code — not a ticker, not a company name
props.reason: The issuer name and title are identical, and match the name of one of the candidate companies.
props.verdict: Three characters of overlap, and nothing else. This row has no right answer to get.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week5.json — failures[2], golden-set row g0320

beats.narration_text: Here is the part that changes next week. Three hundred and twenty-two answers, and the model reported full confidence on three hundred and fifteen of them. Twelve of the fifteen answers that disagree with the labels came back at ninety-five percent or higher. It was completely sure, and it was wrong. So next week's review queue cannot be sorted by the model's confidence. That was the plan.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w5-confidence.png. The errors must read as sitting INSIDE the confident mass — that adjacency is the finding.

show.event: 322 dots fill the field, one per answer, in scoring order.

show.at: on 'full confidence on three hundred and fifteen'
show.event: The 1.000 block lights as one mass; the count resolves to 315.
The disagreeing dots ring terracotta — INSIDE the confident block, not outside it.
The consequence line lands across the foot.

props.title: Confidence does not sort them
props.subtitle: one dot per answer, 322 answers, ordered as scored
props.distinctNote: The model only ever returned 1.00, 0.95, 0.00 — three values, for 322 different questions.
props.consequence: A review queue sorted by confidence would put twelve of the fifteen errors at the bottom.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week5.json — dots[], one entry per adjudicated golden-set row

beats.narration_text: One thing did work. Every mistake was the model adding a company. The single time it helped, it took one away. So I built a version allowed only to veto, never to propose. It scores a perfect one point oh, on four rows. Four. I built it, measured it, and left it switched off. It is a decent sceptic and a poor proposer.

shot.visual_intent: Rebuild of pantry/w5-veto.png. The sample size must be as loud as the score, or the beat becomes the boast it is arguing against.

show.event: Two direction counters: 14 added, 1 removed.
The four rows land, one per line, with the vetoed row marked.
The 1.0000 sets at display size beside the row count.
SWITCHED OFF stamps across the metric, and the caveat lands beneath.

props.sparkLine: Built it, measured it, left it off.
props.eyebrow: WEEK 5 · THE THING I TURNED OFF
props.title: Every row the veto would ever see
props.subtitle: the LLM allowed only to REMOVE a claim, never to add one
props.directionNote: Every error ran one way. So take the direction away from it.

rows.name: MWAM VC SPACEX-II, LLC …
rows.note: trailing space in the filed name

props.verdictNote: A perfect score on four rows is not evidence. It is a policy with almost nothing to do. Shipping it would mean quoting 1.0000 and hoping nobody asks the sample size.
props.source: SOURCE: figdata_week5.json — veto_rows[], scoreboard.F_v2_veto. Names shortened at the exposure clause; rows 3 and 4 are the same filed string apart from a trailing space, as noted.

beats.narration_text: Week five on one page. An eight billion parameter model, given exactly what the rules get. Three hundred and twenty-two calls, zero failures, five points of precision gone. One bad record becomes a hundred and ninety-six. Every failure was the same failure, a resemblance promoted to a match, once by inventing a fact outright. Full confidence on three hundred and fifteen answers, including twelve that were wrong. The plan said keep the rules if there is no lift. There is no lift. I am keeping the rules.

show.event: The Claude artifact page opens — Measuring a Local LLM Against the Matcher, week 5.
Five findings stagger in, one per spoken clause.

props.artifactTitle: Measuring a Local LLM Against the Matcher — week 5
artifactLines: llama3.1:8b local, temperature 0, seed 7 — 322 calls, 0 failures, 3.24s each, on the same four fields the rules get.
Precision 0.9959 → 0.9449 on the same 322 labels. Recall unchanged at 1.0000. In records, 1 false positive becomes 196.
Every error ran one way: 14 companies added, 1 removed. One reason was an invented corporate fact — “HYPERSCALE DATA INC … is the parent company of Scale AI, Inc.”
Confidence 1.000 on 315 of 322 answers, and 12 of the 15 disagreements came back at 0.95 or above. A review queue cannot be sorted by it.
Veto-only scores 1.0000 — on 4 rows. Built, measured, switched off. The plan pre-committed: no lift, keep the rules. Keeping the rules.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Take a task you were about to hand to a language model, and write down, before you run it, what result would make you keep what you already have. Then run it and score both on the same cases. And check one thing in particular. When the model is wrong, does it know? If its confidence cannot separate its right answers from its wrong ones, you have not bought a reviewer. You have bought more work.

Then score both systems on the same labelled cases, and test whether the model's own confidence separates its right answers from its wrong ones.
